newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CNA-Gallo leaps on Pick'n Pay buy rumours.
newsitem.headline: CNA-Gallo leaps on Pick'n Pay buy rumours.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's music to retailing group CNA-Gallo Ltd jumped on Tuesday on rumours that stores firm Pick'n Pay Ltd was in talks to buy it, dealers said.
The rumours envisage Pick'n Pay buying the whole group and then keeping the CNA retail chain and selling the Gallo entertainment arm.
"I think it is really going to happen," one dealer said.
At 0950 GMT CNA-Gallo shares were up 49 cents, or 12.69 percent, to a new year high of 435 cents -- the biggest climber on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
Pick'n Pay shares were up 20 cents to match their year high of 720 cents.
Raymond Ackerman, chairman of Pick 'n Pay, said the firm would consider looking at buying into the group CNA-Gallo.
"It is not completely nonsense...if CNA came up for sale we certainly would investigate it," he told Reuters.
But Ackerman added that the idea of a buy was still speculation.

"It really is total rumour. But we do have our PNA stationers and the matter has been mooted...We are considering options on a lot of issues on how to pursue PNA and I think that this is how it must have come up," he said.
A spokeswoman for CNA-Gallo said that the firm was trading under a cautionary announcement warning shareholders it was in talks that may effect its share price and that it would be renewed on Friday.
But she added the firm did not comment on market rumours.
"No one here can say anything," she said.
Late last month Premier Group Ltd, a major shareholder of CNA-Gallo, said that it was considering unbundling the unit and splitting it.
"We think it is probably going to be more appropriate to split and unbundle that business," Premier chairman Doug Band told an analysts' briefing.
CNA-Gallo operates a retail arm as well as the NuMetro chain of cinema's and Band said any split of the firm would divide it into separate retail and entertainment businesses.

The firm said on May 27 that a merchant bank was assessing ways to restructure the group to enable it to capitalise on its entertainment operations, which have overtaken the retail division in contribution to earnings.
